title: Pattern: Simple Conversational Prompt Format
description:
## Context
When creating .prompt.md files for GitHub Copilot Chat

## Problem
Complex nested headers (##, ###) cause:
- VS Code UI navigation issues (prompts show as navigable sections)
- Prompts read like technical specs vs actionable instructions
- Hard to maintain, users struggle to understand purpose

## Solution
Use simple, conversational instructions with minimal structure
- No heading hierarchy - just frontmatter + plain text/bullets
- Conversational tone: "Review X for Y" not "This prompt reviews X..."
- Action-focused: Tell AI what to do, not how prompt works
- Brief: 10-15 lines ideal, 20 max

## Example
```markdown
---
description: 'Brief, clear'
agent: specialized-agent
tools: ['codebase', 'search']
---

Review code for quality and best practices.

title: Pattern: Plug-In Architecture - Detect Don't Prescribe
description:
Context: Toolkit integrates with ANY frontend project without requiring tool changes

Problem: Recommending specific tools (Vite, Jest, etc.) creates adoption barriers. Users shouldn't need to migrate tooling.

Solution: Always DETECT existing tools first, then adapt recommendations. Check package.json for build tool, test framework, frontend framework.

Example:
- Bad: Install Vite for your build tool
- Good: I see you're using Webpack. Let's optimize webpack.config.js...
- Good: No test framework detected. If needed, Vitest is a modern choice, though Jest works too

Universal Tools (Always Safe):
- Lighthouse CLI - works with any project
- axe-core - framework-agnostic a11y
- Browser DevTools - universal debugging

When to Use: Writing tool-specific guidance, providing code examples, suggesting optimizations

Rationale: Toolkit should ENHANCE existing projects, not require rebuilding them
